claims.claim: The GitHub v3.6.0 release is commit 7c56a5e40f7fd928dfd5c72902d5def0097db73a and was published on 2026-01-21 UTC.

evidence.locator: release header
evidence.observation: The upstream release page identifies v3.6.0, short commit 7c56a5e, and publication at 21 Jan 23:27.

challenge.alternative: The date refers only to a later documentation update or another tag.
challenge.check: Inspect the signed upstream v3.6.0 release header and resolve the tag with git ls-remote.
challenge.outcome: Both identify the same v3.6.0 commit and release publication.

claims.claim: Triton 3.6 was the first release with native Blackwell tcgen05/TMEM lowering; through Triton 3.5 the compiler only emitted Hopper WGMMA and kept accumulators in registers.

evidence.locator: TTNG_TCGen5MMAOp, TTNG_TCGen5MMAScaledOp, TTNG_TMEMLoadOp, TTNG_TMEMStoreOp, TTNG_TMEMAllocOp, TTNG_TMEMCopyOp
evidence.observation: The v3.3.0 dialect defines native TCGen5 MMA and TMEM operations; TMEMCopy explicitly lowers to tcgen05.cp.

evidence.locator: Blackwell lowering CHECK directives
evidence.observation: Pinned tests require tcgen05.mma, tcgen05.commit, TMEM encodings, scaled MMA, and cta_group::2 output.

evidence.locator: new Blackwell dialect, lowering, allocation, and test files
evidence.observation: The version boundary adds MMAv5 lowering, tensor-memory allocation, and Blackwell lowering tests; the corresponding symbols are absent at v3.2.0.

challenge.alternative: The v3.3 symbols are dead scaffolding while real compilation still emits only WGMMA.
challenge.check: Inspect v3.3's conversion tests and MMAv5 lowering files, and compare their absence at v3.2.
challenge.outcome: The pinned v3.3 tests check concrete tcgen05 PTX forms, directly contradicting the claimed 3.6 first-support boundary.

claims.claim: Triton 3.6 incrementally expands the existing Blackwell backend with generic tcgen05.cp, more generic TMEM/ld/st layouts, tcgen05.mma layout generalization, aref warp-specialization work, and initial Gluon multi-CTA/2CTA support.

evidence.locator: Backend & Compiler lines 221-225; NVIDIA Backend lines 310-340; Gluon lines 351-389
evidence.observation: The release enumerates generic tcgen05.cp, TMEM layout changes, tcgen05.mma generalization, warp-specialization aref work, initial 2CTA/multi-CTA, num_ctas, and scaled MMA support.

challenge.alternative: These items are a wholesale first implementation rather than refinements.
challenge.check: Compare the 3.6 release items with the pinned v3.3 and v3.5 dialect/tests and release notes.
challenge.outcome: Earlier releases already contain TCGen5/TMEM lowering; the listed 3.6 changes are narrower additions and generalizations.

claims.claim: By Triton 3.5, Blackwell paths include persistent-matmul and fused-attention warp specialization, generic tcgen05.ld/st exposure, block-scaled matmul, and an explicit Gluon tcgen05/TMEM tutorial.

evidence.locator: NVIDIA Backend, Hopper/Blackwell Features and Blackwell-Specific
evidence.observation: The release notes enable warp specialization for persistent matmul and FA and list TMEM, tcgen05_copy, generic tcgen05.ld/st, and tcgen05.commit work.

evidence.locator: tutorial introduction, tmem_example_kernel, and small_mma_kernel
evidence.observation: The tutorial allocates/loads/stores TMEM and invokes tcgen05_mma on Blackwell.

evidence.locator: Blackwell block-scaled matmul tutorial
evidence.observation: The v3.5 tree already ships the tl.dot_scaled Blackwell tutorial.

challenge.alternative: Those user-visible examples appear only after the v3.5 tag.
challenge.check: Open the files and release notes at the exact v3.5 commit.
challenge.outcome: The tagged v3.5 tree contains the tutorial files and implementation references.

claims.claim: The page's 'when to use' bullets are recommendations; their concrete examples are grounded by actual Triton attention, GatedDeltaNet projection, format-conversion, normalization, dot_scaled, and warp-specialized matmul code, but the page provides no benchmark scope for its CuTe-DSL turnaround comparison.

evidence.revision: verbatim bundles at SHAs a1257fd1, 890df95b, 766d225f, 5bdc07d9, and 5638d40f
evidence.locator: the six files linked in original units u048-u053 and their PROVENANCE.yaml entries
evidence.observation: Pinned code contains Triton JIT kernels for the named workload categories. No unit or cited benchmark defines or measures 'turnaround' against CuTe DSL.

challenge.alternative: The bullets report a scoped comparative benchmark rather than editorial guidance.
challenge.check: Inspect the bullets, cited source trail, and performance table columns.
challenge.outcome: They contain no workload, machine, software revision, timed region, trials, or turnaround measurements.

claims.claim: The 'use alternatives' introduction is editorial guidance rather than a universal benchmark result; the two following bullets give specific downstream cases.

evidence.observation: The imperative heading is followed by one SGLang benchmark report and one routing decision, not a universal performance table.

challenge.alternative: The heading itself is an independently quantified claim for all workloads.
challenge.check: Inspect its grammatical form and the scope of the two supporting units.
challenge.outcome: It is a recommendation whose factual support is limited to the two named cases.

claims.claim: SGLang PR 5390 reports 10,447.34 total tok/s for its CUTLASS MLA run versus 8,227.35 tok/s for its Triton run (26.98% higher), and PR 21595 changes the SM100 multimodal-attention default from triton_attn to FA4.

evidence.locator: Deepseek-R1 Benchmarks, CUTLASS and Triton result blocks
evidence.observation: The PR records the commands, 3,000 prompts, token lengths, dtype, TP/DP settings, and the two reported throughput totals; this verifies only what that PR reports, not a universal speedup.

evidence.locator: Summary and commit 'Restrict fa4 default to Blackwell SM100 only'
evidence.observation: The PR explicitly changes the Blackwell datacenter SM100 default from triton_attn to fa4 while retaining other defaults by architecture.

challenge.alternative: The percentage compares different metrics or the routing change applies to every GPU.
challenge.check: Use the total-token-throughput rows for both PR 5390 runs and the architecture-scoped summary of PR 21595.
challenge.outcome: 10447.34/8227.35-1 is 26.98%, and the routing PR explicitly restricts the change to SM100.

claims.claim: The page correctly cautions that plain tl.dot lowering and every tutorial/downstream shape are not proved by the cited downstream artifacts.

evidence.locator: whole file; tl.dot sites around lines 358, 372, and 399
evidence.observation: The artifact contains tl.dot kernels but no PTX dump, tcgen05 name, TMEM operation, warp_specialize argument, or lowering record.

challenge.alternative: The downstream artifact itself contains inspectable tcgen05 PTX proving every tl.dot path.
challenge.check: Search the provenance-pinned artifact for tcgen05, TMEM, PTX, and warp_specialize and compare to a positive-control Triton v3.5 tcgen05 tutorial.
challenge.outcome: The downstream file has none of those lowering witnesses; the positive control does.

claims.claim: vLLM PR 34597 is an SM100-only production-decode anchor that demonstrates its tl.dot kernels lower through Triton 3.6's tcgen05/TMEM path.

evidence.locator: PR summary and changed files
evidence.observation: The PR adds FP8 KV-cache support to a generic Triton MLA backend and describes that backend as the only MLA option on SM120; it does not identify an SM100-only path or tcgen05 lowering.

evidence.locator: kernel definitions and tl.dot call sites
evidence.observation: The code contains tl.dot but no architecture guard, Triton-version requirement, warp_specialize, tcgen05, TMEM, or emitted PTX evidence.

challenge.alternative: Architecture metadata outside the code proves it is SM100-only and its tl.dot necessarily emits tcgen05.
challenge.check: Inspect the primary PR body, exact changed code, and its guards/imports.
challenge.outcome: The primary source mentions SM120 and supplies no lowering witness, contradicting the SM100-only/demonstration framing.

claims.claim: vLLM PR 34597 genuinely modifies an @triton.jit MLA decode kernel with tl.dot operations and adds FP8 KV-cache support, with two verbatim files pinned locally at merge SHA a1257fd1.

evidence.locator: PROVENANCE.yaml; triton_decode_attention.py decorators and tl.dot call sites; triton_mla.py supported_kv_cache_dtypes
evidence.observation: The provenance lists exact hashes; the code contains Triton kernels and the stated tl.dot operations, while the backend file adds FP8 cache dtypes.

challenge.alternative: The bundle is a derived excerpt or contains only a dispatch gate.
challenge.check: Verify asset_mode, upstream paths, SHA-256 values, decorators, and dot call sites.
challenge.outcome: Both files are marked verbatim and contain the implementation described, though they do not prove a particular backend lowering.

claims.claim: vLLM PR 29339 gates triton_kernels MXFP4 use to SM90 and SM100 and changes only the dispatch file mxfp4.py.

evidence.locator: PR title, motivation, and changed files
evidence.observation: The upstream PR limits triton_kernels to SM90/SM100 for MXFP4 and lists only vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py.

challenge.alternative: The PR adds a new Triton kernel or proves TCGen5 code generation.
challenge.check: Inspect its one-file diff and changed-files list.
challenge.outcome: It is a dispatch gate, not a kernel or lowering proof.

claims.claim: Pinned SGLang artifacts show a GatedDeltaNet fused projection implemented with Triton loads/stores and an extend-attention kernel implemented with Triton dot products.

evidence.locator: @triton.jit kernels and tl.load/tl.store sites
evidence.observation: The verbatim file implements fused QKVZBA split/reshape/cat projection through Triton memory operations and contains no tl.dot.

evidence.locator: @triton.jit extend-attention kernels and tl.dot call sites
evidence.observation: The verbatim file performs QK, QPE/KPE, and probability/value dot products.

challenge.alternative: The page swapped which artifact contains matrix products.
challenge.check: Search each exact file for decorators, tl.dot, tl.load, and tl.store.
challenge.outcome: The GDN projection is load/store rearrangement; extend_attention contains the dot products, matching the narrowed claim.

claims.claim: The local downstream artifacts do not contain an explicit tcgen05 PTX dump or a warp-specialized descriptor/TMA lowering witness.

evidence.environment: GNU ripgrep over provenance-pinned local artifacts
evidence.reference: A lowering witness would contain a TCGen5/TMEM/PTX term or explicit warp-specialize surface.
evidence.result: No matching lowering witness was found in the three cited downstream bundles.
evidence.negative_control: The same terms match Triton v3.5.0's python/tutorials/gluon/06-tcgen05.py and compiler sources.

challenge.alternative: The absence result is caused by a broken search pattern.
challenge.check: Run the identical search against the pinned upstream positive control.
challenge.outcome: The positive control matches, so the search discriminates the downstream artifacts.

claims.claim: The live FlashInfer-Bench author leaderboard displays 0.628x/73.1% for gemini-2.5-pro, 0.467x/92.3% for gpt-5-2025-08-07, and 0.456x/73.1% for claude-opus-4-1-20250805 across 660 workloads.

claims.claim: Those FlashInfer-Bench rows are a preserved Triton-3.5-era snapshot that specifically measures AI-generated Triton kernels, and no Triton 3.6 rerun is available.

evidence.locator: Leaderboard rows and labels
evidence.observation: The current live page still shows the values but labels them only by author, speedup, resolved percentage, and workload count; it supplies no Triton version, historical-snapshot date, or Triton-only language filter.

challenge.alternative: Hidden table metadata pins these exact rows to Triton 3.5 and marks a missing 3.6 rerun.

claims.claim: The gated_delta_net_decode block is a usable Triton kernel implementing its stated recurrent-state update.

evidence.command: conda run -n base python -c <AST undefined-name audit over the two wiki Python blocks>
evidence.environment: Conda base, Python 3.13.14, host AST analysis
evidence.reference: A self-contained kernel must define every loaded local name or receive it as an argument.
evidence.result: gated_delta_net_decode loads undefined name offsets; its state/output address expressions are also inconsistent between load and store.
evidence.negative_control: A well-scoped control function taking offsets and d as arguments reports no undefined names.

challenge.alternative: offsets is an implicit Triton builtin.
challenge.check: Compare the function arguments and Triton language namespace with the AST load set.
challenge.outcome: offsets is neither an argument, assignment, nor tl builtin, so the displayed function cannot compile as written.

claims.claim: The sparse_attention_fwd block is a usable Triton sparse-attention kernel.

evidence.command: conda run -n base python -c <AST undefined-name audit over the two wiki Python blocks>
evidence.environment: Conda base, Python 3.13.14, host AST analysis
evidence.reference: A self-contained kernel must define every loaded local name or receive it as an argument and must write its promised output.
evidence.result: sparse_attention_fwd loads undefined d and offsets, stops at an unfinished softmax comment, and never stores Output.
evidence.negative_control: A well-scoped control function taking offsets and d as arguments reports no undefined names.

challenge.alternative: d and offsets are compiler-provided names and the omitted store is outside the excerpt by design.
challenge.check: Inspect the complete fenced block, signature, and loaded names.
challenge.outcome: The block closes without defining the names or producing Output, so it is incomplete executable-looking code.

claims.claim: CPU launch overhead can materially affect short-kernel workflows; CUDA Graphs reduce repeated CPU launch costs, and vLLM at commit a1257fd1 defaults to FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs and has GDN decode graph support.

evidence.locator: 4.2 CUDA Graphs introduction
evidence.observation: The guide states that per-kernel host setup is significant for short kernels and graphs reduce CPU launch costs by preparing work in advance.

evidence.locator: CUDAGraphMode and CompilationConfig.cudagraph_mode documentation
evidence.observation: FULL_AND_PIECEWISE is documented as the v1 default and most performant mode for most models.

evidence.locator: GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder and build_for_cudagraph_capture
evidence.observation: The GDN backend advertises uniform-batch graph support and implements decode-only full graph capture.

challenge.alternative: CUDA Graphs are unrelated to launch overhead or GDN opts out of vLLM's default graph path.
challenge.check: Inspect the CUDA guide plus the pinned compilation default and GDN metadata builder.
challenge.outcome: The sources directly connect graphs to CPU launch cost and explicitly implement GDN decode graph capture.
